atoms.text: Easter is one of the most important holidays for Christians. Easter is a holiday celebrating when Jesus Christ rose from the dead three days after his crucifixion. Christians believe that Jesus Christ died for their sins. This holiday is most commonly celebrated between the end of March and the middle of April. However, Orthodox Christians celebrate Easter between April and May. Before Easter, many families go to church to get food blessed for Easter Sunday. At Easter, families get together, eat lots of food, go to church and some hide Easter eggs.

atoms.text: Yom Kippur is one of the most important Jewish holidays. This holiday happens in either September or October and is after Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year. During this time Jews ask for forgiveness for sins that they committed in the previous year. They believe that during the 10 days before Yom Kippur, God judges all creatures. During this holiday, adults go to the synagogue and fast from sunrise to sunset. This means they do not eat food or drink water while the sun is up. This is a way of cleansing the body for the next year.
